scene:
Three zones read left to right, separated by generous space.

LEFT ZONE (the widest), one need split three ways: at the top left a small office building with a stack of coins beside it, labelled ROTALINE NEEDS €100K. From it three arrows fan out to three stacked route cards, top to bottom. Top card: three small customer figures handing over a coin, with a calendar icon, labelled CUSTOMER PREPAYMENT, and under it a smaller label DELIVER BY 1 MARCH; this card carries a large ochre check mark and a stamp labelled CHOSEN. Middle card: a bank building with a monthly calendar of repeating coins, labelled BANK LOAN, with a smaller label €3,040 A MONTH. Bottom card: a blank share certificate and an empty chair at a board table, labelled NEW SHARES, with a smaller label 10% + BOARD SEAT.

MIDDLE ZONE, two small contrasting flow diagrams stacked vertically. Upper diagram: an investor figure hands a coin along a teal arrow to a company building, labelled ISSUED SHARES: CASH TO COMPANY. Lower diagram: an investor figure hands a coin along an ochre arrow to a founder figure standing beside (not inside) the company building, which gets nothing, labelled EXISTING SHARES: CASH TO SELLER.

RIGHT ZONE, a checklist clipboard with three question rows (no numerals), each with a small icon: a hand receiving a coin labelled WHO RECEIVES THE CASH?; a blank document with a small chain labelled WHAT IS OWED?; a pen over a signature line labelled WHO APPROVES SPENDING?

All coins are plain discs with no symbols; draw no dollar, euro or other currency signs on any object. Figures, buildings, documents and furniture carry no words, letters or numerals of their own; people are unlabelled.

TEXT: draw exactly these labels, each once and nothing else: ROTALINE NEEDS €100K, CUSTOMER PREPAYMENT, DELIVER BY 1 MARCH, CHOSEN, BANK LOAN, €3,040 A MONTH, NEW SHARES, 10% + BOARD SEAT, ISSUED SHARES: CASH TO COMPANY, EXISTING SHARES: CASH TO SELLER, WHO RECEIVES THE CASH?, WHAT IS OWED?, WHO APPROVES SPENDING? Any other text is a defect.
alt: Rotaline's €100,000 need fans out to three routes: a customer prepayment that must be delivered by 1 March (chosen), a bank loan costing €3,040 a month, and new shares giving up 10% and a board seat; issued shares put cash into the company while existing shares pay the seller; a clipboard asks who receives the cash, what is owed and who approves spending.
caption: The same €100,000 from three sources, three different promises, and the three questions to ask of any funding.
